ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 81
ayahs.arabicText: بَلْ قَالُوْا مِثْلَ مَا قَالَ الْاَوَّلُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: Nay, but they say like their predecessors of yore had said.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 82
ayahs.arabicText: قَالُوْۤا ءَاِذَا مِتْنَا وَ كُنَّا تُرَابًا وَّ عِظَامًا ءَاِنَّا لَمَبْعُوْثُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: They say: 'Is it that when we are dead and have been reduced to dust and bones, shall we then be raised up again?

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 83
ayahs.arabicText: لَقَدْ وُعِدْنَا نَحْنُ وَ اٰبَآؤُنَا هٰذَا مِنْ قَبْلُ اِنْ هٰذَاۤ اِلَّاۤ اَسَاطِیْرُ الْاَوَّلِیْنَ
ayahs.translation: We were promised such things and so were our forefathers before us. All these are no more than tales of the past."
ayahs.commentary: . Their denial of the life after death implied the denial of the powers and wisdom of Allah as well.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 84
ayahs.arabicText: قُلْ لِّمَنِ الْاَرْضُ وَ مَنْ فِیْهَاۤ اِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: Ask them: 'Whose is the earth and who are those who are in it? Tell us if you know.'

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 85
ayahs.arabicText: سَیَقُوْلُوْنَ لِلّٰهِ١ؕ قُلْ اَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: They will surely say: "Allah's." Say: "Then why do you not take heed?"
ayahs.commentary: . That is, if you acknowledge this, why do you not then understand that none but Allah deserves to be worshiped and that when He has once created the earth and all the things in it, it is not difficult for Him to re-create them once again?

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 86
ayahs.arabicText: قُلْ مَنْ رَّبُّ السَّمٰوٰتِ السَّبْعِ وَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِیْمِ
ayahs.translation: Ask them: 'Who is the Lord of the seven heavens, the Lord of the Great Throne?'

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 87
ayahs.arabicText: سَیَقُوْلُوْنَ لِلّٰهِ١ؕ قُلْ اَفَلَا تَتَّقُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: They will surely say: "Allah." Say: "Will you not, then, fear (Allah)?"
ayahs.commentary: . See (E.N. of this Surah). . That is, why are you not afraid of rebelling against Him and worshiping others besides Him? Why do you not dread that one day you shall have to give an account of all your deeds to the All-Powerful Sovereign of the universe?

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 88
ayahs.arabicText: قُلْ مَنْۢ بِیَدِهٖ مَلَكُوْتُ كُلِّ شَیْءٍ وَّ هُوَ یُجِیْرُ وَ لَا یُجَارُ عَلَیْهِ اِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: Ask them: "Say, if you indeed know, to whom belongs the dominion over all things; (Who is it) that grants asylum, but against Whom no asylum is available?"
ayahs.commentary: . The word malakut in the text is a strong word which combines both sovereignty and ownership. The verse therefore means: Whose is the Sovereignty and Who possesses the real ownership rights over everything?

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 89
ayahs.arabicText: سَیَقُوْلُوْنَ لِلّٰهِ١ؕ قُلْ فَاَنّٰى تُسْحَرُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: They will surely say: "(The dominion over all things) belongs to Allah." Say: "Whence are you then deluded?"
ayahs.commentary: . In order to understand the significance of this question, we should know that the art of magic makes a thing appear different from what it really is. Thus the question will mean: Who has bewitched you that, in spite of knowing and acknowledging all these things, you do not understand the reality? Who has bewitched you that even after acknowledging Allah to be the Owner and the All-Powerful Sovereign, you set up other owners and sovereigns along with Him or make them partners with Him and worship them? Who has deluded you that you should dare to be treacherous and unfaithful to Allah knowing that none can protect you against Him, and forget that you will be called to account for these things? In this connection, it should also be noted that this question has a subtle meaning also. The Quraish accused the Prophet (peace be upon him) of practicing magic and sorcery. This question turns the tables on them, as if to say, O people, the man who presents the reality appears to you to be a sorcerer, while those leaders who say things against reality, against common sense and against your own convictions and beliefs, do not appear to you to be sorcerers at all.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 90
ayahs.arabicText: بَلْ اَتَیْنٰهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ وَ اِنَّهُمْ لَكٰذِبُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: We have brought before them the Truth, and there is no doubt that they are lying.
ayahs.commentary: . They are liars because they say that others besides Allah have a share in His Godhead and that there is no life after death, because their first saying contradicts their own admission that Allah is the Owner and the Sovereign of the universe. Then their second assertion is based on the presumption that the All-Powerful Allah cannot recreate what He has created once. This is clearly a contradiction in terms.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 91
ayahs.arabicText: مَا اتَّخَذَ اللّٰهُ مِنْ وَّلَدٍ وَّ مَا كَانَ مَعَهٗ مِنْ اِلٰهٍ اِذًا لَّذَهَبَ كُلُّ اِلٰهٍۭ بِمَا خَلَقَ وَ لَعَلَا بَعْضُهُمْ عَلٰى بَعْضٍ١ؕ سُبْحٰنَ اللّٰهِ عَمَّا یَصِفُوْنَۙ
ayahs.translation: Never did Allah take unto Himself any son, nor is there any god other than He. (Had there been any other gods) each god would have taken his creatures away with him, and each would have rushed to overpower the other. Glory be to Allah from all that they characterize Him with!
ayahs.commentary: . It should be, noted that this is a general refutation of the belief that Allah has a child or children, and incidentally refutes the Christian belief that Christ is the son of God. Yet even some eminent commentators confine this to the refutation of the Christian belief. Obviously, there is no reason why it was necessary to refute the Christian belief specifically in this context, when the whole discourse has been directed towards the disbelievers of Makkah alone, who were, like the Christians, guilty of this sort of shirk. . Here the argument of Tauhid is based on this principle: Had there been more than one God or partners in Godhead, there would have been serious differences, conflicts and wars among the different sovereigns and rulers. See (Surah Bani Israil, Ayat and E.N. ) thereof, and (Surah Al-Anbiya, Ayat and E. N. )thereof.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 92
ayahs.arabicText: عٰلِمِ الْغَیْبِ وَ الشَّهَادَةِ فَتَعٰلٰى عَمَّا یُشْرِكُوْنَ۠ ۧ
ayahs.translation: He knows both what is visible and what is not visible. Exalted is Allah above all that they associate with Him.
ayahs.commentary: . This contains a subtle allusion to the refutation of the doctrine of intercession. See (E.Ns , of Surah Ta-Ha) and (E.N. of Surah AI-Anbiya).

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 93
ayahs.arabicText: قُلْ رَّبِّ اِمَّا تُرِیَنِّیْ مَا یُوْعَدُوْنَۙ
ayahs.translation: Pray (O Muhammad!): 'My Lord, if You should bring the scourge of which they had been warned in my presence,

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 94
ayahs.arabicText: رَبِّ فَلَا تَجْعَلْنِیْ فِی الْقَوْمِ الظّٰلِمِیْنَ
ayahs.translation: then do not include me, my Lord, among these wrong-doing people."
ayahs.commentary: . This prayer does not mean that, God forbid, there was any real danger of the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) also being involved in the punishment, or that if he had not invoked this prayer, he might have been involed in it. This way of address has been adopted to warn that all people should fear Allah’s punishment. They should not demand it nor persist in their wickedness, if Allah gives them respite. As a matter of fact, Allah’s punishment is a thing which should be dreaded not only by the sinful people but also by the righteous people, and they should all seek His refuge from it, for when the scourge of God comes, it does not destroy only the wicked people but may also involve the righteous people in it. Therefore the right course for those, who have to live in a wicked society, is that they should always pray to Allah for His refuge, for one does not know when that scourge might come down.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 95
ayahs.arabicText: وَ اِنَّا عَلٰۤى اَنْ نُّرِیَكَ مَا نَعِدُهُمْ لَقٰدِرُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: Surely We are able to show you that We warn them against.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 96
ayahs.arabicText: اِدْفَعْ بِالَّتِیْ هِیَ اَحْسَنُ السَّیِّئَةَ١ؕ نَحْنُ اَعْلَمُ بِمَا یَصِفُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: (O Muhammad!): Repel evil in the best manner. We are well aware of all that they say about you.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 97
ayahs.arabicText: وَ قُلْ رَّبِّ اَعُوْذُ بِكَ مِنْ هَمَزٰتِ الشَّیٰطِیْنِۙ
ayahs.translation: And pray: 'My Lord! I seek your refuge from the suggestions of the evil ones;

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 98
ayahs.arabicText: وَ اَعُوْذُ بِكَ رَبِّ اَنْ یَّحْضُرُوْنِ
ayahs.translation: I even seek Your refuge, my Lord, lest they should approach me."
ayahs.commentary: . For explanation, see (E.Ns , of Surah Al-Anaam); (E.Ns , to of Surah Al-Aaraf); (E.N. of Surah Younus); (E.N. of Surah Al-Hijr); (E.Ns to of Surah An-Nahl); (E.Ns to of Surah Bani-Israil) and (E.Ns to of Surah HaMim-Sajdah).

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 99
ayahs.arabicText: حَتّٰۤى اِذَا جَآءَ اَحَدَهُمُ الْمَوْتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ارْجِعُوْنِۙ
ayahs.translation: (They shall persist in their deeds) until when death comes to anyone of them he will say: "My Lord, send me back to the world
ayahs.commentary: . In the original text plural number has been used for Allah, which may be for reverence, or may include the angels as well, who will be seizing the criminal soul. The entreaty would be: O my Lord! Send me back.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 100
ayahs.arabicText: لَعَلِّیْۤ اَعْمَلُ صَالِحًا فِیْمَا تَرَكْتُ كَلَّا١ؕ اِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قَآئِلُهَا١ؕ وَ مِنْ وَّرَآئِهِمْ بَرْزَخٌ اِلٰى یَوْمِ یُبْعَثُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: that I have left behind. I am likely to do good." Nay, it is merely a word that he is uttering. There is a barrier behind all of them (who are dead) until the Day when they will be raised up.
ayahs.commentary: . It occurs at several places in the Quran that each of the criminals, after his death till his entry into Hell, and even after that, will plead again and again: Lord, send me back to the world, I will no more disobey Thee, I will now do righteous deeds. See (Surah Al-Anaam, Ayats , ); (Surah Al-Aaraf, Ayat ); (Surah Ibrahim, Ayats , ); (Surah Ash-Shuara, Ayat ); (Surah Al-Fatir, Ayat ); (Surah Az- Zumar, Ayats , ); (Surah Al-Momin, Ayats -), and (Surah Ash-Shura, Ayats )along with the relevant E.Ns. . That is, he will never be sent back nor given another opportunity, for in that case the test and trial for which man is sent to this world becomes meaningless. For further explanation, see (Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayat and E. N. )thereof, and E.Ns , , of Surah Al-Anaam) and (E.N. of Surah Younus). . That is, now, when he has met his doom, he has nothing more to say than that he should be sent back to the world; so let him say what he likes; he will never be allowed to go back. . That is, now there is a barrier between them and the world, which will not allow them to go back to it. Therefore they shall remain in that state until the Day of Resurrection.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 101
ayahs.arabicText: فَاِذَا نُفِخَ فِی الصُّوْرِ فَلَاۤ اَنْسَابَ بَیْنَهُمْ یَوْمَئِذٍ وَّ لَا یَتَسَآءَلُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: And then no sooner the Trumpet is blown than there will remain no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask one another.
ayahs.commentary: . It does not mean that the father will not remain father and the son will not remain son, etc. It only means that they will not be able to help each other, nor shall they be able to inquire about each other as father and son, for each one will be worried and anxious about his own plight. See (Surah Al-Maarij, Ayats -), and (Surah Abasa, Ayats - ).

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 102
ayahs.arabicText: فَمَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِیْنُهٗ فَاُولٰٓئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: It will be an Hour when those whose scales are heavy, they alone will attain success;
ayahs.commentary: . That is, those whose good deeds will be heavy and will out-weigh their evil deeds.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 103
ayahs.arabicText: وَ مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِیْنُهٗ فَاُولٰٓئِكَ الَّذِیْنَ خَسِرُوْۤا اَنْفُسَهُمْ فِیْ جَهَنَّمَ خٰلِدُوْنَۚ
ayahs.translation: and those whose scales are light, those will be the ones who will have courted loss. They will abide in Hell.
ayahs.commentary: . For the criterion of success and failure in the Hereafter, please refer to(E.Ns and )above.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 104
ayahs.arabicText: تَلْفَحُ وُجُوْهَهُمُ النَّارُ وَ هُمْ فِیْهَا كٰلِحُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: The Fire shall scorch their faces, exposing their jaws.
ayahs.commentary: . The word kalih means a face whose skin has been removed so as to expose the jaws. When somebody asked Abdullah bin Masud the meaning of kalih, he said: Haven’t you seen the scorched head of a slaughtered animal?

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 105
ayahs.arabicText: اَلَمْ تَكُنْ اٰیٰتِیْ تُتْلٰى عَلَیْكُمْ فَكُنْتُمْ بِهَا تُكَذِّبُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: Are you not those to whom My revelations were recited, and you dubbed them as lies?'

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 106
ayahs.arabicText: قَالُوْا رَبَّنَا غَلَبَتْ عَلَیْنَا شِقْوَتُنَا وَ كُنَّا قَوْمًا ضَآلِّیْنَ
ayahs.translation: They will say: 'Our Lord! Our misfortune prevailed over us. We were indeed an erring people.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 107
ayahs.arabicText: رَبَّنَاۤ اَخْرِجْنَا مِنْهَا فَاِنْ عُدْنَا فَاِنَّا ظٰلِمُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: Our Lord! Take us out of this. Then if we revert (to evil-doing) we shall indeed be wrong-doers.'

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 108
ayahs.arabicText: قَالَ اخْسَئُوْا فِیْهَا وَ لَا تُكَلِّمُوْنِ
ayahs.translation: Allah will say: "Away from Me; stay where you are and do not address Me.
ayahs.commentary: .“Do not speak to Me”: Do not plead your case with Me. According to some traditions, these will be their last words and they shall never be allowed to speak again, but this is contradicted by the Quran itself in the succeeding verses. Therefore, it only means this that they will not be able to plead their case again.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 109
ayahs.arabicText: اِنَّهٗ كَانَ فَرِیْقٌ مِّنْ عِبَادِیْ یَقُوْلُوْنَ رَبَّنَاۤ اٰمَنَّا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَ ارْحَمْنَا وَ اَنْتَ خَیْرُ الرّٰحِمِیْنَۚۖ
ayahs.translation: Your are those that when a party of My servants said:“Our Lord, we believe, so forgive us, and have mercy on us, for You are the Best of those that are merciful”

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 110
ayahs.arabicText: فَاتَّخَذْتُمُوْهُمْ سِخْرِیًّا حَتّٰۤى اَنْسَوْكُمْ ذِكْرِیْ وَ كُنْتُمْ مِّنْهُمْ تَضْحَكُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: you made a laughing-stock of them and your hostility to them caused you to forget Me, and you simply kept laughing.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 111
ayahs.arabicText: اِنِّیْ جَزَیْتُهُمُ الْیَوْمَ بِمَا صَبَرُوْۤا١ۙ اَنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْفَآئِزُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: Lo! I have rewarded them this Day for their steadfastness, so that they, and they alone, are triumphant."
ayahs.commentary: . This is again a reference to those who will deserve success or be doomed to failure in the Hereafter.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 112
ayahs.arabicText: قٰلَ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ فِی الْاَرْضِ عَدَدَ سِنِیْنَ
ayahs.translation: Then Allah will ask them: 'For how many years did you stay on the earth?'

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 113
ayahs.arabicText: قَالُوْا لَبِثْنَا یَوْمًا اَوْ بَعْضَ یَوْمٍ فَسْئَلِ الْعَآدِّیْنَ
ayahs.translation: They will say: "We stayed for a day or part of a day. Ask of those who keep count of this."
ayahs.commentary: . For explanation, see (Surah Ta-Ha Ayat and E.N. ) thereof.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 114
ayahs.arabicText: قٰلَ اِنْ لَّبِثْتُمْ اِلَّا قَلِیْلًا لَّوْ اَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: He will say: "You stayed only for a while, if you only knew that.
ayahs.commentary: . That is, Our Messengers warned you that the life in this world is transitory and is for test and trial, but you did not realize it then and denied that there was any life in the Hereafter and behaved in accordance with that belief.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 115
ayahs.arabicText: اَفَحَسِبْتُمْ اَنَّمَا خَلَقْنٰكُمْ عَبَثًا وَّ اَنَّكُمْ اِلَیْنَا لَا تُرْجَعُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: Did you imagine that We created you without any purpose, and that you will not be brought back to Us?"
ayahs.commentary: . The Arabic word abathan in the text also means“for the sake of sport”. Then the verse will mean: Did you think that We had created you merely for the sake of sport and there was no purpose behind your creation? Therefore you may eat, drink, be merry and enjoy yourself as you please.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 116
ayahs.arabicText: فَتَعٰلَى اللّٰهُ الْمَلِكُ الْحَقُّ١ۚ لَاۤ اِلٰهَ اِلَّا هُوَ١ۚ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِیْمِ
ayahs.translation: So, exalted be Allah, the True King! There is no god but He, the Lord of the Great Throne.
ayahs.commentary: . Allah is above this that He should create you without any purpose and that you may associate partners with Him with impunity.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 117
ayahs.arabicText: وَ مَنْ یَّدْعُ مَعَ اللّٰهِ اِلٰهًا اٰخَرَ١ۙ لَا بُرْهَانَ لَهٗ بِهٖ١ۙ فَاِنَّمَا حِسَابُهٗ عِنْدَ رَبِّهٖ١ؕ اِنَّهٗ لَا یُفْلِحُ الْكٰفِرُوْنَ
ayahs.translation: He who invokes any other god along with Allah " one for whom he has no evidence" his reckoning is with his Lord alone. Indeed, these unbelievers shall not prosper.
ayahs.commentary: . It may also be translated as: The one who invokes any other deity along with Allah, has nothing to support him in this act. . That is, he cannot escape accountability. . Again, the reference is to those who will attain the success and to those who will be deprived of it.

ayahs.title: Tafheem-ul-Quran (En) - Al-Muminoon : 118
ayahs.arabicText: وَ قُلْ رَّبِّ اغْفِرْ وَ ارْحَمْ وَ اَنْتَ خَیْرُ الرّٰحِمِیْنَ۠ ۧ
ayahs.translation: And say, (O Muhammad): "My Lord, forgive us and have mercy on us, for You are the Best of those that are merciful."
ayahs.commentary: . Compare and contrast this prayer with (verse ). Here the Prophet (peace be upon him) has been told to make the same prayer as contained in (verse ), as if to say, You (and your followers) should supplicate Allah with the same prayer so that, if the people scoff at you, they themselves might provide a proof of a strong case against themselves.
